clue.text: It comes out (and is in) day after 8 (part 2)'s day

indicators.note: after puts the flower part of the name behind the feast-day part

parts.note: the second part of 8 is ARCHANGEL; the archangel Michael's feast day is Michaelmas, 29 September

indicators.note: in places the word is inside the word day

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coy riddle about something emerging on a saint's day, with cross-references to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas is the Christian feast of St Michael the Archangel, 29 September, when this aster typically flowers; the brackets hide the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is said to come out when it blooms, and this autumn aster blooms around late September.

clue.text: Moderate 'ero?

parts.note: the three letters ERO sit at the very centre of the two words THE ROAD, so they are literally that phrase's middle

explanation.walkthrough: Write out THE ROAD: its seven letters have E, R, O in the middle, so 'ero is the centre of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle-of-the-road politician or view is moderate, avoiding extremes either side.

clue.text: Small seal on one front cover of volume

parts.note: a young seal can be called a cub
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: front signals that only the first letter of cover is wanted

explanation.surface: A baby seal resting on the front of a book's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic is the adjective for measurements of volume, as in cubic metres.

clue.text: The opposite of two marks

parts.note: Mark Antony, so a Mark can be ANTONY
M is the abbreviation for the mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what is the reverse of a pair of marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase gives two different marks: the Roman Mark Antony and the German currency M.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, so it is literally an opposite.

clue.text: Description of "Jaws" might be magic

definitions.meaning: ... jaws are long, thin jaws giving a hollow-cheeked face
a magic ... is an early image projector

explanation.surface: A film reviewer calling the shark movie magical.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantern is the word in both the phrase lantern-jawed and the old projector called a magic lantern.

clue.text: Artistic place for raised line in a row

indicators.note: in tells us the raised line goes inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
an el is an elevated railway, a line carried up on stilts

explanation.surface: Someone searching for the arty spot to put a raised line among a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised line' looks like a written underline, but an EL is the American term for an elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop or studio.

clue.text: Dead treetop's somehow damper

indicators.note: somehow tells us the letters of top are jumbled

parts.note: a tree is an ash, followed by top as written; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A dead treetop being somehow wetter than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treetop' must be split into tree and top; 'somehow' then mixes the ASH TOP letters so the top becomes a POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashpot is a mechanical damper, a piston in fluid that slows movement.

clue.text: Swallowing what's told jokingly over there

indicators.note: told means the words are spoken aloud and we write what we hear

parts.note: jokingly is in jest, and over there is the old word yon

explanation.surface: Gulping down a joke someone told across the room.
explanation.walkthrough: IN JEST plus YON, spoken aloud, gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingestion is the act of taking food or drink into the body, that is swallowing.

clue.text: Cry o' battle to shift large plant

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
o' is a short form of of, giving the letter O
a war is a battle
to change is to shift

explanation.surface: A battle cry ordering troops to move a big plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow archangel is a woodland plant of the dead-nettle family with yellow flowers.

clue.text: Poet takes pipe back for new one

indicators.note: takes means the poet holds the next piece inside him

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet

indicators.note: back means the word for pipe is read backwards

parts.note: a tube is a pipe

explanation.surface: A poet takes back his pipe in exchange for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the pipe; 'new one' means a newcomer, here to high society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman newly presented in society, so a new one in that world.

clue.text: Mark of magic when small watch doesn't start

indicators.note: doesn't start removes the first letter of the word for watch

parts.note: a vigil is a watch kept through the night

explanation.surface: A magical mark appears when a small watch fails to start.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigil is a sign or symbol believed to have magical power.

clue.text: Gallic ensemble having to give permission

indicators.note: having signals that the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A French band needing to grant permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To license is to authorise or grant permission formally; the s spelling is the verb in British use.

clue.text: Child with regard for thick paint

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
as to means with regard to

explanation.surface: A child respectfully considering some thick paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on thickly so that brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: Soft or hard, depending on sex …

definitions.text: Soft or hard, depending on sex …

parts.words: Soft or hard, depending on sex
parts.note: fish eggs are called hard when from the female and soft (milt) when from the male

explanation.surface: Something whose firmness depends on gender, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and soft are the standard names for the female eggs and male milt of fish.

clue.text: … and what he's asked to do

definitions.text: … and what he's asked to do

parts.words: and what he's asked to do
parts.note: following on from the previous clue, the word for fish eggs sounds like the thing this man is asked to do with a boat

explanation.surface: A continuation from the previous clue about a man and his task.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous answer, said aloud, sounds like 'row', which is exactly what a rower in a crew is asked to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman is a person who rows a boat, and rowing is what he is asked to do.

clue.text: Way to be impressed by sunrise's form — or lack of it?

indicators.note: to be impressed by is to be pressed into, so the road goes inside the reshaped letters
form tells us to rearrange the letters of sunrise into a new shape

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a road should be struck by the shape of the dawn, or by its absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges SUNRISE into RUINESS; 'be impressed by' puts ST into it. 'it' in the definition is form, as in an athlete's form.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustiness is lack of form or practice, as in a player out of condition.

clue.text: Bend in the centre of 8

indicators.note: the centre of picks out the three letters at the very middle of answer 8

parts.note: 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, the woodland plant, whose fifteen letters are taken

explanation.surface: A bend in the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference: count to the eighth of the fifteen letters of 8 down and take it with its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curve, a bend shaped like part of a circle.

clue.text: Ruminater's drink?

parts.note: the letters of Ruminater's are rum plus a jumble of this Greek wine, so it is fancifully his drink

explanation.walkthrough: RUMINATERS breaks into RUM plus INATERS, which rearranges to the answer: a cryptic hint with no explicit anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, so a drink.

clue.text: Times are changing

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters of are are rearranged

explanation.surface: The times are changing.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of time, so times as in the times we live in.

clue.text: Dense group of society that's short in the tooth

indicators.note: in places the shortened society inside the long tooth

parts.note: a tusk is a long tooth
Soc is the short form of society

explanation.surface: A dense crowd from society, a little long in the tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'long in the tooth', but 'short' here trims the word society to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense clump or tuft of grass.

clue.text: Start to sing in opera performance outside

parts.note: to open is to start
an air is a tune or song to be sung, as in an opera

explanation.surface: Striking up a song in an opera staged in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN OPERA also rearrange to the answer, a neat bonus in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means outdoors, so outside.

clue.text: Punish rugby forwards holding up three-quarters

indicators.note: holding means the forwards wrap around the quarters
up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the pack is the forwards in rugby
N, E and E are three compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Disciplining the rugby pack for delaying the three-quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, three-quarters are backs, but here they are three compass quarters N, E, E. 'up' turns PACK into KCAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneecap is to shoot someone in the knee as punishment, a paramilitary practice.

clue.text: Editor's so consumed by article about Dickens

indicators.note: consumed means the editor's word takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: sic is the word an editor inserts meaning so written
at can mean by, as in at the door
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor absorbed in an article about Charles Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dickens' is an old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the dickens'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means relating to the devil, and the dickens is a mild name for the devil.

clue.text: M-mare's t-trotting, say

indicators.note: trotting suggests the letters jogging into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse is trotting, written with stuttering letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself stammers; rearrange M, MARES and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating initial letters like M-m and t-t is exactly what a stammer sounds like.

clue.text: One needs an interior upheaval for this phenomenon

indicators.note: an upheaval churns the pieces around, rearranging their letters

parts.note: must means needs to
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thing that needs an inner upheaval to occur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior upheaval' scrambles I, MUST and AN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a natural phenomenon, a great wave caused by an undersea upheaval.

clue.text: Fool any number with it

parts.note: N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A fool with any number of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Nit, short for nitwit, is British slang for a fool.

clue.text: Impressive points of both sexes

parts.note: epic means grand or impressive
E, N and E are compass points

explanation.surface: Impressive features of both men and women.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having characteristics of both sexes, or neither.

clue.text: Barbs don't fly in such cases

definitions.text: Barbs don't fly in such cases

parts.words: Barbs don't fly in such cases
parts.note: barbs are small tropical fish kept in tanks, rather than cutting remarks flying about

explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks for fish, such as barbs, which stay put inside them.

clue.text: Check statement as a rule

indicators.note: statement means the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: to rein in is to check

explanation.surface: Checking that a statement is generally true.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch.

clue.text: Some game shows last

indicators.note: shows means the letters appear inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Some game shows run for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it means the last.

clue.text: Contrasting arrival with standard entry

indicators.note: entry signals the standard goes into the arrival

parts.note: a coming is an arrival
par is the standard level

explanation.surface: Judging an arrival against standard entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparing things means setting them side by side to note contrasts.

clue.text: I'd poor part — lion's share when 29

definitions.text: I'd poor part — lion's share when 29

indicators.note: share suggests the letters being divided up and dealt out afresh

explanation.surface: A complaint about getting a poor part while the lion takes the biggest share.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is COMPARING: the lion's share is out of proportion when compared to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of proportion describes the lion's share, far bigger than anyone else's part.
